Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY engine.mjs sdk.mjs server.mjs meter-config.example.json ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json CONFIG=/app/meter-config.example.json
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# Meter Keeper

Usage metering for small SaaS teams that bill through Stripe. Your app sends
usage events; Meter Keeper counts each exactly once, prices the month, tells
your app when a customer is over a limit, and feeds
[Stripe Billing Meters](https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based)
with retries. MIT, one Node process, no dependencies, state in a JSON file.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/meter-keeper/

Try your pricing on real usage numbers first: open `index.html` (nothing is
uploaded; the page makes no network requests).

## Why use this instead of what you have today

| Today | Problem for a small team | Meter Keeper |
|---|---|---|
| Lago, Orb, Metronome, OpenMeter, Amberflo | Full billing platforms, or per-event fees, or a database cluster to run | One process, one file, no per-event fee. Not a billing platform: Stripe still invoices |
| Stripe Billing Meters alone | Counts and bills, but has no per-customer "what will they owe", no limit check for your app, and a dropped call is a lost charge | Local source of truth, invoice previews, `/v1/check`, a retry queue and a visible dead-letter list |
| A counter in your own database | Double counts on retry, no tiers, rebuilt for every product | Idempotent on event id, four pricing models, tested |

If you need invoicing, tax, proration and a customer portal in one product, use
a billing platform. This is the counting layer for teams that stay on Stripe.

## Run it

```
cp meter-config.example.json meter-config.json
API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) node server.mjs
```

It starts in `DRY_RUN=true`: events are metered and priced locally and nothing
goes to Stripe. Environment:

| Variable | What |
|---|---|
| `API_KEY`, `ADMIN_KEY` | required, 16+ characters; the first is for your app, the second for you |
| `CONFIG` / `CONFIG_JSON` | meters and plans (file path, default `./meter-config.json`; or the JSON inline) |
| `STATE` | state file, default `/tmp/state.json`; put it on a disk |
| `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` | restricted key allowed to write Billing Meter Events |
| `DRY_RUN` | `false` to send to Stripe |

### Config

A **meter** has an `agg`: `sum` (add the values), `count` (events, value ignored),
`max` (peak value, e.g. storage GB) or `unique` (distinct `key`, e.g. active
users). Add `stripeEvent` to forward it to the Stripe meter of that event name.
A **plan** has an optional `base` and `minimum` (cents) and `lines`, each a
`meter` with a `model`: `flat` (`unit` cents), `graduated`, `volume` (`tiers`
with `upTo` and `unit`, last `upTo: null`), or `package` (`unit` per `size`
units), plus `included` free units and an optional hard `limit`. Tier limits
count units after the included ones. See `meter-config.example.json`.

### API

All `/v1/*` calls take `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY`.

- `POST /v1/events` with `{id, customer, meter, value?, timestamp?, key?}` or
  `{events: [...]}` (1-100). Per-event status `accepted`, `duplicate` or
  `rejected`. The `id` makes retries safe. Timestamps must be within 35 days
  past and 5 minutes ahead, the window Stripe accepts.
- `GET /v1/usage?customer=&meter=&from=&to=`
- `GET /v1/invoice-preview?customer=` the month so far, in cents
- `GET /v1/projection?customer=` straight-line guess for the full month
- `GET /v1/check?customer=&meter=&quantity=` is this call inside the plan limit?

Admin calls take `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY`. `GET /v1/admin/overview`
lists every customer with this month's invoice, the projection, and each line's
percent of its hard limit, plus the total and the customers at 80% or more.

### SDK (Node 18+, server side)

Your own server serves a tiny client at `/sdk.mjs`. It buffers `track()` calls,
sends them in batches, and retries with the same event ids, so a lost response
cannot double count. It never throws into your request path, and `check()`
fails open if the meter is unreachable.

```js
import { createMeter } from "https://meter.example.com/sdk.mjs";
const meter = createMeter({ url: "https://meter.example.com", key: process.env.METER_API_KEY });
meter.track("acme", "api", 1);
if (!(await meter.check("acme", "api")).allowed) return res.status(402).end();
await meter.close(); // flush on shutdown
```

Keep the key on the server: it can read every customer's usage.

Admin calls take `$ADMIN_KEY`: `PUT /v1/admin/customers/:id` with
`{plan, stripeCustomerId}`, `GET /v1/admin/customers`, `GET /v1/admin/outbox`
(pending and dead-lettered Stripe events), `POST /v1/admin/flush`,
`GET /v1/admin/export.csv`.

### Limit alerts

Set `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` (and `ALERT_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) and the server POSTs JSON
to your URL the first time a customer reaches 80% and 100% of a plan line's
`limit` in a month (`"alerts": {"at": [0.5, 0.9, 1]}` in the config changes the
thresholds). One alert per customer, meter, month and threshold. Body:
`{type: "usage.threshold", customer, plan, meter, threshold, used, limit, month, resetsAt}`.
`x-meter-signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body>` is sent when a secret
is set; verify it before trusting the call. Failed deliveries retry with
backoff, then land in the dead-letter list. Without a URL, no alerts are kept.

### Stripe

Create a Billing Meter whose event name matches `stripeEvent`, with `sum`
aggregation (a `unique` meter forwards one event per key per month, value 1).
The event id is sent as Stripe's `identifier`, so a retry cannot double count.
Events that cannot be delivered (customer without a `stripeCustomerId`, Stripe
4xx) land in the dead-letter list; check it at least weekly, because Stripe
drops events older than 35 days.

## One-click deploy

Fork this repository, then open
`https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>` (the blueprint is
`render.yaml`; Render bills you, nothing runs on the author's account). Or use
the repository-wide deploy page. Docker: `API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) docker compose up -d` from this directory
(`docker-compose.yml`, starts in dry-run). Fly.io: the steps are at the top of
`fly.toml`.

## Limits

State is one JSON file rewritten on every write: fine for thousands of events a
day, not for millions. Events within the last 14 months are kept as per-day
totals, not individually. There is no tax, proration or invoicing. Invoice
previews are calculations from what this server saw, not invoices.

## Tests

`node --test`

## Disclaimer

Free and MIT, provided as-is with no warranty and no uptime guarantee. You run
it, so you are responsible for what you charge, for backups and for your
customers' privacy: send ids you choose, not names or emails. Not legal, tax or
financial advice. If it helps, [sponsor the author](https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood).

owner: duncan

docker-compose.yml.text:
# Any box with Docker:
#   API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) docker compose up -d
# Starts in DRY_RUN=true with the example meters. Put your own meters in a file, mount it and set CONFIG,
# then add STRIPE_SECRET_KEY and DRY_RUN=false to forward usage to Stripe.
services:
  meter-keeper:
    build: .
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["8080:8080"]
    volumes: ["state:/data"]
    environment:
      STATE: /data/state.json
      API_KEY: ${API_KEY:?set API_KEY (16+ characters)}
      ADMIN_KEY: ${ADMIN_KEY:?set ADMIN_KEY (16+ characters)}
      CONFIG_JSON: ${CONFIG_JSON:-}
      DRY_RUN: ${DRY_RUN:-true}
      STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: ${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY:-}
volumes:
  state:

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   (DRY_RUN stays true until you add DRY_RUN=false and STRIPE_SECRET_KEY; set your meters with CONFIG_JSON)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: a stopped server drops the usage events your app sends.
app = "meter-keeper-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"
  DRY_RUN = "true"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Charge for usage without building a billing system.

Meter Keeper is an open-source usage meter for small SaaS teams that bill through Stripe. Your app sends events; it counts each one exactly once, prices the month, tells your app when a customer is over a limit, and feeds Stripe Billing Meters with retries. You run it in your own account. First, try your pricing against real usage numbers. Everything runs in your browser, so nothing you paste is uploaded.

1. Price a month of usage

CustomerUnitsBillPer 1,000 units

Models: flat (unit), graduated (each tier priced at its own rate), volume (the whole quantity at the rate of the tier it lands in; tiers may carry a flat fee) and package (unit per block of size). Tier limits count units after the included ones. Look at the right-hand column: if your biggest customers pay far less per unit than your smallest, that is the discount you chose.

2. Run the meter yourself

git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo && cd oss-monorepo/ventures/meter-keeper
cp meter-config.example.json meter-config.json      # your meters and plans
API_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) node server.mjs   # DRY_RUN=true until you change it

curl -X POST localhost:8080/v1/events -H "authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -d '{"id":"req_8f3a","customer":"acme","meter":"api_calls","value":1}'

Send the same id twice and the second is a harmless duplicate. Read back with GET /v1/usage, /v1/invoice-preview, /v1/projection and /v1/check?customer=acme&meter=api_calls&quantity=1 (does this call fit the plan's limit?). To feed Stripe, create a Billing Meter with the same event name, give the server a restricted key that can write meter events, and set DRY_RUN=false. One-click Render deploy and Docker are in the README.

Questions

Why not use Lago, OpenMeter, Orb or Metronome?

Those are good products and the right choice if you need invoicing, tax and a full billing platform. Meter Keeper does one narrow job for a small team that already bills through Stripe: count usage exactly once, price it, enforce limits, and feed Stripe Billing Meters. It is one dependency-free Node process with a JSON file for state, so there is nothing to operate. If you outgrow it, your events are plain JSON you can replay elsewhere.

What stops an event being counted twice?

Every event carries an id you choose. Sending the same id again is reported as a duplicate and changes nothing, so your client can retry freely after a timeout. The same id is passed to Stripe as the meter event identifier, so a retry from this server cannot double-bill either.

What happens when Stripe is down?

Events are stored first and forwarded after, from a queue. A 5xx or rate-limit answer is retried with a growing delay for up to eight tries. A permanent error, such as a customer with no Stripe id, goes to a visible dead-letter list instead of vanishing. Stripe only accepts events up to 35 days old, so look at the queue at least weekly.

Which pricing models are supported?

Flat per unit, graduated tiers, volume tiers, and package pricing (a price per block of N units), each with free included units, an optional base fee, a monthly minimum and a hard usage limit. The invoice preview is a calculation from the usage this server has seen, not the invoice: your Stripe prices stay the source of truth for what a customer is charged.

Is it safe to put real customer data in?

Store only ids you choose, never names or emails. You run the server, so you are responsible for securing the API key, backing up the state file and following the privacy and tax rules where you and your customers live.

Same buyer, other jobs: Drip Keeper sends lifecycle email, Dunning Engine recovers failed payments, MRR Pulse shows MRR and churn, License Keeper issues license keys and Waitlist Keeper runs a launch waitlist.

No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. You are the operator of your meter: you are responsible for the accuracy of what you send it, for what you charge your customers, and for backups. Invoice previews and projections are calculations, not invoices, and are not legal, tax, or financial advice. Everything on this page runs in your browser: nothing you enter is uploaded and the page makes no network requests. Usage counters (opt-out below) stay in your browser's local storage.

Sponsor on GitHub ·

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
# Starts in DRY_RUN=true with the example meters. Set CONFIG_JSON to your own meters and plans, then add
# STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (a restricted key that can write Billing Meter Events) and set DRY_RUN=false to forward usage to Stripe.
services:
  - type: web
    name: meter-keeper
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/meter-keeper
    dockerfilePath: ventures/meter-keeper/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: API_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: CONFIG_JSON
        sync: false
      - key: DRY_RUN
        value: "true"
      - key: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
        sync: false
